newsitem.title: USA: Comcast in talks on sports network link.
newsitem.headline: Comcast in talks on sports network link.

text.p: Comcast Corp. President Brian Roberts said Wednesday the company was in talks with three television sports networks about a possible affiliation with its planned Philadelphia sports channel.
Roberts told reporters after addressing a Montgomery Securities conference that the discussions were under way with the Fox-Liberty, ESPN and CNN/SI networks.

He said a deal would likely involve a so-called "backdrop," in which the local channel would use the national name and some of its programming. It is unlikely that an investment would be involved in any arrangement, he said.

Comcast is a majority owner of the Philadelphia Flyers professional hockey team and Philadfelphia 76ers basketball team. The company plans to launch a local sports channel in October, which would feature games played by those teams as well as by the Philadelphia Phillies baseball team. Comcast bought the rights to air the Phillies games.

Fox/Liberty Networks agreed to pay $850 million for a 40 percent stake in Rainbow Media Holdings Inc., which is 75 percent owned by Comcast and 25 percent by General Electric Co.'s NBC unit, with 25 percent, the companies said Monday.
The companies would form a joint venture in a bid to create a new national sports network.

Fox-Liberty is owned by News Corp. Ltd. and Liberty Media Corp., a unit of Tele-Communications Inc. ESPN is jointly owned by Walt Disney Co. and privately held HearstCorp. CNN/SI is owned by Time Warner Inc.
